name: 2N7000
description: N-channel enhancement-mode small-signal MOSFET in TO-92, 60V / 200mA. Low-power switching, level shifting, and signal interfacing. Threshold 0.8-3.0V, but Rds(on) is rated at Vgs=10V, so it is not a true logic-level part at 3.3V despite the low threshold.

pins.name: S
pins.description: source; usually to ground/common in low-side switching

extra.Rds_on: 5 ohm max at Vgs=10V (6 ohm at Vgs=4.5V)

typical_application: Logic-driven switching of relays/LEDs/small loads under 200mA, level shifting, and signal interfacing.
gotchas: pinout is S-G-D (pin1=Source), the REVERSE of the BS170 (D-G-S); they look identical but are NOT pin-compatible drop-ins
not a true logic-level FET: Rds(on) is rated at Vgs=10V; at 3.3-5V drive it conducts but with higher Rds(on) and cannot reach full current
Vgs absolute max is only +/-20V; static or gate transients can punch the thin gate oxide
modest 200mA / 350mW; easy to exceed with inductive loads or sustained current
